translation_notes: Translated: the two plain-predicate equalities (`g.value(a, RBDYN_COORD["as-seen-by"]) == g.value(b, GEOM_COORD["as-seen-by"])`) -> `m{ {a} rbdyn_coord:as-seen-by ?v }.first() == m{ {b} geom_coord:as-seen-by ?v }.first()`; the seven `QUDT_UNIT["X"] in self.g[s : QUDT_SCHEMA["unit"]]` slice-membership asserts -> `bool(m{ {s} qudt_schema:unit qudt_unit:X })` (an existence test, trav_existence); the four `self.g.add` on the shared subject `id_` -> a single `+{ {id_} a rbdyn_op:InertialWrench ; ... }` (the draft's `self.g += g{ }` replaced), with `@graph self.g` as first line. The project's `kindynsyn.namespaces` (DefinedNamespace classes) is imported both ways: `from ... import geom_coord:, rbdyn_coord:, rbdyn_op:, qudt_schema:, qudt_unit:` for islands and the original name import, kept, for the path reads below.

NOT expressible, four of the six value equalities: `self.g.value(s, RBDYN_COORD["of-inertia"] / RBDYN_ENT["about"])` -- the predicate is an rdflib property PATH (URIRef / URIRef), and `m{ }` has no property paths. Interpolating the Path (`m{ {s} {RBDYN_COORD["of-inertia"] / RBDYN_ENT["about"]} ?v }.first()`) does not raise: it silently matches nothing and gives None (verified: the same graph answers urn:c through `g.value`), which makes `None == None` assertions pass -- a silent wrong answer, not an error. The only island that could do it is `s{ SELECT ?v WHERE { {s} p1/p2 ?v } }`, which has no `.first()` and no single-value reduction. The four reads are therefore left as `self.g.value(..)` on both sides (rdflib), so 4 of the 6 reads of the stratum are not covered.

A second lexical finding: the vocabulary's local names are hyphenated (`of-inertia`, `as-seen-by`, `M-KiloGM`, `RAD-PER-SEC`). Inside an island Turtle's character set applies and `rbdyn_coord:of-inertia` is a name; OUTSIDE an island `-` is subtraction (`p = rbdyn_coord:of-inertia` -> NameError: inertia), and inside a `{...}` interpolation the code is Python too. So a hyphenated name can only be written in a pattern; in an expression (the path above) one must fall back to `RBDYN_COORD["of-inertia"]`, which forces keeping the Python-name import beside the prefix import.

Context shim: the real kindynsyn package is not installed; `kindynsyn/namespaces.py` and `kindynsyn/rdflib_tools/helpers.py` are verbatim copies of comp-rob2b/kindyngen@414ebd52b2 (the two `__init__.py` are reduced to a comment: the real ones re-export subpackages the region does not use). `uuid_ref()` is random: the driver replaces `uuid.uuid4` by a deterministic counter in the driver process before the sides fork.

Driver: `A failed assert raises a bare AssertionError()` -- the same value whichever of the thirteen asserts failed -- so `self` is a class instance whose `g` is a `ReadLog` (real Graph recording the (subject, predicate) of every pattern the REGION asks; frames of the harness's own post-call reads are excluded) and whose `reads` list is compared as an argument mutation: the log stops where the run stops. The object position is left out because `o in g[s:p]` scans (s, p, None) while the island's existence test asks (s, p, o): same question, not the same call. 27 calls: consistent triples; one edit per assertion (13); a unit present only as qudt:quantityKind; a unit held by another subject; None == None cases (missing on both sides); two as-seen-by values in both orders (first read counts); the as-seen-by moved to the other namespace; empty graph; unknown subjects. Mutation checks: geom_coord for rbdyn_coord on one as-seen-by, and qudt:unit -> qudt:quantityKind on one unit assert, both FAIL; restored.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: `g = self.g` once. The six value equalities, whose left side is always rigid_body_inertia, become a table of (inertia path, other subject, other path) and one assert in a loop. The seven unit assertions become a table of (subject, unit local name) and one assert. The four adds on id_ become one `g += [...]`. Non-hyphenated names use attribute access (`RDF.type`, `QUDT_SCHEMA.unit`, `RBDYN_ENT.about`, `GEOM_REL.of`, `RBDYN_OP.wrench`).

The reads keep their order and their number: the driver logs every (subject, predicate) the region asks, so the duplicated as-seen-by read of rigid_body_inertia is not factored out. Every assert keeps its bare AssertionError. The path objects are built before the first read, which changes nothing (they read nothing and the names are defined).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g`, one `+{ {id_} a rbdyn_op:InertialWrench ; ... }` for the four triples, and `qudt_schema:unit` in the unit slice. The hyphenated path components (`of-inertia`, `as-seen-by`, ...) cannot be prefixed names outside an island, and rbdyn_ent:/geom_rel: are not imported by the translated header, so the equality table stays Python on both sides.

Rule 4: the value reads stay `g.value(...)`, shorter than `m{ {s} {path} ?v }.first()` even now that an interpolated path is evaluated. In the unit loop `QUDT_UNIT[unit] in g[subject : qudt_schema:unit]` is shorter than `m{ {subject} qudt_schema:unit {QUDT_UNIT[unit]} }` (10 tokens against 12).

Metric observation: `+{ ... }(g)` with a call suffix is measured 5 tokens heavier than `@graph g` plus `+{ ... }` (the island text then ends with `)`, so tokenize_island skips its body handling and hyphenated names are split). `@graph g` is the shorter form in any case.
No exception to the symmetry: both table loops are pure Python and are in both files.
header_optimization_notes: Python: collection, BNode, Literal, GEOM_ENT and QUDT_QKIND go; RDF, the seven namespace classes the region reads and uuid_ref stay.

LD Python: the whole rdflib import goes (the type is `a`). RBDYN_OP, QUDT_SCHEMA, GEOM_ENT and QUDT_QKIND go, and so do the unused prefix imports geom_coord:, rbdyn_coord: and qudt_unit:. The five namespace classes still used and the two prefixes rbdyn_op: and qudt_schema: share one import statement.
